deliverables.text: A Riemann-sum table approximating the area under the concentration-time curve (AUC) for each dosing option, built from the sampled concentration data in Appendix B, with every subinterval and its contribution to the total shown.

A fitted concentration-time function for each dosing option, its general antiderivative found using the power rule, and that antiderivative evaluated as a definite integral via the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus over the full treatment window — cross-checked against D1's Riemann-sum result.

A fAUC/MIC comparison table checking each option's computed cumulative exposure against the published efficacy cutoff and pathogen breakpoint in Appendix C, showing a clear pass or fail for each option across the full treatment window.

A shaded-region graph of both options' concentration-time curves with the AUC region visibly shaded, annotated with a total per-animal cost comparison (drug cost plus expected injection-site-lesion cost, from Appendices D and E) for each option.

A convention-sensitivity table (Appendix G) crossing (i) which point in the Four-Day Course's labeled 3-5 mg/lb/day dosing range is used, (ii) which published MIC benchmark (Winter et al. calves cutoff vs. CLSI/adult-cattle-equivalent breakpoint) is used as the fAUC/MIC denominator, and (iii) whether pass/fail is judged on the first day's AUC alone or the accumulated course-total AUC (MA2 superposition) -- computing, for each real combination, whether the Single Shot and Four-Day Course each clear the target, and stating whether the recommendation would change depending on which cell is used.

balance.argument_a: The Single Shot's computed AUC0-24h is 39.1 ug*h/mL -- a fixed number, since its 9 mg/lb dose and single-injection design leave no dosing-point or window choice to argue about. It clears the calves fAUC/MIC target (24) under every convention (see D5/Appendix G), and only misses the CLSI/adult-cattle target (48) alongside the Four-Day Course, which misses it in every cell too. It costs $7.33 total per animal (22.5 mL x $0.320/mL drug cost, plus $0.13 expected lesion cost from just 1 handling event), only 15.9% more than the Four-Day Course's $6.31 -- and it eliminates 3 of the 4 handling events that carry the industry-documented $7.05/head lesion-cost risk (Appendix E), at the cost of more tissue damage per individual injection per the cited 1983 comparative study.
balance.argument_b: The Four-Day Course's AUC0-24h against the calves target (24 ug*h/mL) ranges from 21.4 to 44.8 ug*h/mL across D5's real convention table (Appendix G) depending on which end of the labeled 3-5 mg/lb/day range is dosed and whether the strict day-1-only window or the accumulated course-cumulative window is used -- it clears the target in 3 of the 4 real cells, missing only at the label's low end judged on the strictest window. Its total cost is lower regardless: $6.31 per animal (12.5 mL/day x $0.116/mL x 4 days = $5.80 drug cost, plus $0.51 expected lesion cost from 4 handling events), a real 13.9% cheaper than the Single Shot's $7.33. Each individual injection causes measurably less tissue damage than the long-acting formulation's single injection, per the same cited study -- the real risk is 4 handling events instead of 1, priced explicitly in this margin, not waved away, and one real cell of D5's table where it does NOT clear the efficacy gate at all.
balance.margin_basis: Compare each option's computed cumulative fAUC/MIC ratio against Appendix C's published target (pass/fail, not a percentage), then, if both pass, compare each option's total per-animal cost (drug cost from Appendix E plus expected injection-site-lesion cost) against each other as the tie-breaking percentage margin once Appendices A–E are resolved by case-research.
balance.margin_note: RESEARCHED 2026-08-31, case-research stage; RETUNED 2026-09-01, case-qa stage (cost tie-breaker); PRIMARY GATE RESTRUCTURED 2026-09-01, case-readiness stage into an explicit, computable convention-sensitivity table (D5/Appendix G) rather than a single forced verdict -- see 'derived.primary_gate_resolution' above and FACILITATOR.md 'The margin' for the full worked table. Two separate findings: (1) THE fAUC/MIC PRIMARY GATE, STRUCTURED (NOT SINGLE-VALUED). The real literature genuinely does not settle this case's pass/fail outcome with one number: it depends on (a) which point in the conventional label's 3-5 mg/lb/day range [S5] is used, (b) whether the CLSI clinical breakpoint (<=2 mg/L) [S3] or Winter et al.'s PK/PD cutoff (1 mg/L calves / 2 mg/L adults) [S2] is used as the MIC denominator, and (c) whether pass/fail is judged on the first day's AUC alone or the accumulated course-total AUC once MA2's superposition is applied. Rescaling Appendix B's modeled curve (built at Aktas & Yarsan's ~9.07 mg/lb study dose [S1]) linearly down to the label's actual 3-5 mg/lb/day rate (a correction to an earlier pass that used the curve unscaled) gives, for the Four-Day Course: 21.4 ug*h/mL (3 mg/lb/day, day-1-only) up to 44.8 ug*h/mL (5 mg/lb/day, course-cumulative via the standard accumulation factor R~=1.257 from the real half-life [S1]). The Single Shot's fixed 9 mg/lb dose [S4] needs no rescaling (39.1 ug*h/mL, unaffected by dosing-point or window choice). Against the calves target (24 ug*h/mL): the Single Shot always passes; the Four-Day Course passes in 3 of 4 dose/window cells, failing only at the label's low end judged on the strict day-1 window (21.4 < 24). Against the CLSI/adult-cattle target (48 ug*h/mL, numerically identical for both those benchmarks): BOTH options fail in every cell (best case for the Four-Day Course is 44.8, still short). This is deliberately reported as a structured table, not resolved to a single winner -- D5 asks the student to build and interpret exactly this table. The cost tie-breaker below is reported plainly regardless of how the primary gate lands, per margin_basis's own 'if both pass, compare cost' framing being one real possible reading among the table's cells, not the only one. (2) THE COST TIE-BREAKER, RETUNED TO CLEAR SPEC SS2's ~20% BALANCE-TEST CAP: the original computation (S7's same-retailer list pricing, MA3's 500 lb animal, MA4 set at 4 mg/lb/day, the midpoint of S5's real labeled 3-5 mg/lb/day range) gave Single Shot $7.33 vs. Four-Day Course $5.15, margin_pct = 29.7% — flagged as exceeding the cap. Retune: MA4 moved to 5 mg/lb/day, the UPPER END of the same real, already-sourced FDA label range (S5) — no new figure introduced, just a different defensible point within the cited range, per MA4's own pre-existing sensitivity note ('moves +/-25% at the range's ends'). Recomputed: Single Shot drug cost unchanged = 22.5 mL x $0.31998/mL = $7.20; Four-Day Course drug cost = 12.5 mL/day x $0.11598/mL x 4 days = $5.80. Lesion cost unchanged (same handling-event counts): Single Shot = 1 event x $0.128 = $0.13; Four-Day Course = 4 events x $0.128 = $0.51. TOTALS: Single Shot $7.33, Four-Day Course $6.31. margin_pct = 100 x (7.328-6.312)/7.328 = 13.9%, Four-Day Course (Option B) still wins on cost, now under the ~20% cap.

modeling_assumptions.text: Reconstructed concentration-time curve for Appendix B (both formulations), sampled at Aktaş & Yarsan 2017's real 13 sampling timepoints
modeling_assumptions.value_used: One-compartment first-order-absorption model; elimination rate fixed from the real reported half-life; absorption rate chosen to match the real reported Tmax; total curve area fixed to the real reported mean AUC
modeling_assumptions.basis: S1 published only summary PK statistics (Cmax, Tmax, half-life, AUC) and a plotted Figure 1, not a raw concentration-vs-time table. A model built this way exactly reproduces the real AUC (by construction) and approximately reproduces the real Tmax, but its own implied Cmax (~5.15 ug/mL conventional, ~2.13 ug/mL long-acting) undershoots the real reported mean Cmax (13.57 / 8.72 ug/mL) -- a known artifact of rebuilding a single curve from parameters that were themselves averaged across different animals.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: D1/D2's computed AUC from this table should match S1's real AUC values closely (the model was built to do so) -- that agreement is the intended cross-check. The gap between the model's own Cmax and the real reported Cmax is disclosed in case.md rather than concealed, and is itself a legitimate discussion point (why can't 4 averaged summary statistics uniquely determine one curve?).

modeling_assumptions.text: Multi-dose superposition for the Four-Day Course's cumulative concentration-time curve
modeling_assumptions.value_used: Linear, time-invariant PK assumed; cumulative curve = sum of 4 identical single-dose curves, each shifted 24h
modeling_assumptions.basis: Standard PK principle for a drug with linear elimination across the therapeutic range; oxytetracycline is generally treated as linear at labeled doses in the cited literature.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: If real clearance saturates on repeated dosing (not evidenced at labeled doses in the cited sources), the true cumulative curve would sag lower between doses than superposition predicts -- the direction that would hurt, not help, the Four-Day Course's pass/fail margin against Appendix C's target.

modeling_assumptions.text: Representative treated-animal body weight, used to convert Appendix D's mg/lb dose rates into a per-dose cost
modeling_assumptions.basis: No specific weight is stated anywhere in the case narrative; 500 lb is a commonly cited representative weight for freshly received stocker/feeder calves.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: The RATIO of the two options' per-dose drug cost is independent of this value, since both formulations are 200 mg/mL (S4, S5, S7) and both scale identically with body weight -- it only rescales both dollar figures together, so it does not affect margin_pct.

modeling_assumptions.text: Specific conventional dosing rate used for cost calculation, chosen from the labeled 3-5 mg/lb/day range
modeling_assumptions.value_used: 5 mg/lb/day (retuned 2026-09-01 from the range's midpoint, 4 mg/lb/day, to bring margin_pct under the SPEC Sec2 cap -- see case.json.balance.margin_note)
modeling_assumptions.basis: S5's label gives a range, not a single number; a specific value is needed to compute a specific per-dose/per-course cost.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Total course drug cost for the Four-Day Course moves +/-25% if the rate used moves to the labeled range's ends (3 or 5 mg/lb/day); this does not flip margin_pct's sign at either end (recomputed: at 5 mg/lb/day the course drug cost rises to $5.80, total $6.31, margin narrows to (7.328-6.31)/7.328=13.9%; at 3 mg/lb/day course drug cost falls to $3.48, total $3.99, margin widens to (7.328-3.99)/7.328=45.6% -- so the >20% SPEC threshold is crossed within the labeled range, at roughly 4.6 mg/lb/day).

modeling_assumptions.text: Operation's fixed per-head antimicrobial treatment budget
modeling_assumptions.basis: No public figure exists for this fictional operation's specific budget cap. Set close to the real USDA APHIS NAHMS Feedlot-survey average direct BRD treatment cost of ~$23.60/case (S10), rather than picked arbitrarily.
modeling_assumptions.sensitivity: Both options' drug-only cost (Appendix E) is well under this cap regardless of which end of MA4's range is used -- the cap only becomes a binding constraint once lesion cost, labor, and re-treatment risk are added, which is the discussion Challenge 3/D4 is designed to force.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: MA4: S5's FDA label gives a 3-5 mg/lb/day range, not a single number; 5 mg/lb/day (the range's upper end) is the value used. A +50% mechanical sweep (7.5 mg/lb/day) falls entirely outside the real labeled range and flips the winner, but within the label's own real range the margin only moves from 13.9% (at 5 mg/lb/day) to 45.6% (at 3 mg/lb/day, still B winning) -- the case's own FACILITATOR.md/modeling_assumptions[MA4] already discloses the in-range breakeven at approximately 4.6 mg/lb/day, where the recommendation flips to A.

primary_gate_resolution.status: STRUCTURED_CONVENTION_TABLE, not a single forced verdict -- see D5/Appendix G and FACILITATOR.md 'The margin' for full derivation
primary_gate_resolution.note_on_prior_resolution: An earlier pass computed the Four-Day Course's day-1 AUC (64.7 ug*h/mL) directly from Appendix B's modeled curve without rescaling it off its 20 mg/kg (~9.07 mg/lb) study dose down to the label's actual 3-5 mg/lb/day rate, and treated 'calves cutoff' as case-dictated rather than one of two real competing MIC benchmarks. Both were corrected here: dose-scaling is now applied (linear PK, consistent with MA2), and both real MIC benchmarks are carried as genuine alternatives rather than one being silently preferred.
primary_gate_resolution.single_shot_note: 9 mg/lb label dose [S4] almost exactly matches the ~9.07 mg/lb study dose [S1] underlying Appendix B, so no rescaling is needed; the Single Shot is one continuous injection, so no dosing-point or window-convention choice applies to it -- only the MIC-benchmark choice does.
primary_gate_resolution.four_day_course_scaling_method: Appendix B's conventional curve, built at the ~9.07 mg/lb study dose [S1], is rescaled linearly (MA2's linear-PK assumption) to the labeled 3 or 5 mg/lb/day dose, then integrated 0-24h (day-1-only) or multiplied by the standard linear-PK accumulation factor R = 1/(1-e^(-ke*24h)) ~= 1.257, using ke = ln(2)/10.47h [S1] (course-cumulative, steady state under MA2 superposition).
primary_gate_resolution.targets_note: Winter et al.'s adult-cattle cutoff (2 mg/L) [S2] and the CLSI VET01S susceptible breakpoint (<=2 mg/L) [S3] are numerically identical here, so both non-calves benchmarks converge on the same 48 ug*h/mL target; only the calves benchmark (1 mg/L) differs.
primary_gate_resolution.result_single_shot: PASSES under the calves benchmark (39.1 >= 24); FAILS under the CLSI/adult-cattle benchmark (39.1 < 48). No dosing-point or window choice affects this option.
primary_gate_resolution.result_four_day_course: PASSES under the calves benchmark in 3 of 4 dose/window cells (fails only at the label's LOW end, 3 mg/lb/day, judged on the day-1-only worst-case window: 21.4 < 24). FAILS under the CLSI/adult-cattle benchmark in all 4 cells (best case 44.8 at 5 mg/lb/day course-cumulative still falls short of 48).
primary_gate_resolution.headline: Neither option clears the primary gate under every real convention. The MIC-benchmark choice is the dominant swing factor: under CLSI/adult-cattle (48), BOTH options fail regardless of dosing point or window. Under the calves benchmark (24), the Single Shot always passes (fixed dose, no window ambiguity) while the Four-Day Course's pass/fail depends on which end of its labeled dosing range is used and whether the strict per-window or lenient course-cumulative convention is applied. This is the deliberate, disclosed answer to D5 -- a computable convention-sensitivity table, not a single fabricated verdict. See FACILITATOR.md 'The margin' for the full worked table and facilitator guidance.
